Posterior variance components and ICCs

Source: R/utils-scd-analysis.R
bootstrap_variance_components.Rd

Summarizes the residual variance, the random-intercept variance of each grouping factor, and the intraclass correlations from the posterior draws of a fitted model. For each draw, \(ICC_g = \tau_g^2 / (\sum_h \tau_h^2 + \sigma^2)\), where \(\tau_g\) is the intercept SD (sd_<g>__Intercept) of grouping factor \(g\) and \(\sigma^2\) the residual response variance; the residual enters the denominator once. The intervals are posterior quantiles, so they carry the full posterior uncertainty of every variance component.

Usage

bootstrap_variance_components(model, n_boot = 200)

Arguments

model

A brmsfit object.

n_boot

Positive finite integer number of posterior draws summarized (evenly spaced over the chains; all draws when fewer are available).

Value

A list with summary (a matrix with rows mean, sd, ci_lower.2.5%, ci_upper.97.5% and one column per quantity: sigma2, each grouping factor's intercept variance, and iccs.<group>), n_successful (draws used), and n_attempted (n_boot); NULL for a non-brmsfit or when fewer than 10 draws are available.

Details

The name is kept for compatibility. It previously refit the model to posterior-predictive replicates, which double counted the residual and held the case effects at their estimates, so its intervals were too narrow. A parametric bootstrap of a Bayesian multilevel SCD model is unnecessary: the posterior draws already give the distribution of each component. For families without a residual SD (sigma), such as Poisson or negative binomial, or for a model with sigma predictors, the ICCs are NA with a message, since a level-1 variance on the response scale is not a single parameter there. The reported sigma2 includes the Student-t factor nu/(nu - 2). Natural-residual stationary AR(1) models include the factor 1/(1 - ar^2). A covariance-form latent Gaussian AR(1) adds sderr^2/(1 - ar^2) to the independent response variance rather than rescaling its sigma^2. Conditional latent serial models have occasion-dependent boundary variances and return NA; no interior-occasion ICC is substituted. Constant response variances are supported for identity-link Gaussian, Student-t, and skew-normal families only. ICCs are undefined if any retained response SD is nonfinite or negative, if any retained Student-t draw has nu <= 2, if the fitted serial specification cannot establish stationary AR(1), or if the family or link prevents a constant residual response variance. Random-slope models report intercept-reference ratios, not correlations at arbitrary sessions or covariate values.

Examples

if (interactive()) {
fit <- brms::brm(outcome ~ phase + (1 | case), data = simulate_scd_data())
bootstrap_variance_components(fit, n_boot = 1000)
}
